facts.claim: Anatomy indexed from 'Digital Anatomy of Four Music-Marketing Machines' research report (2026-10-03); per-fact evidence tiers and sources recorded in attrs.key_facts

Six official segments: super / moderate / light listeners (active, last 28 days by intensity), previously active (lapsed 28+ days), programmed (heard only via playlists/radio), potential (never heard, profile match)
Segments are built from the listener behavior graph: stream counts, intentional vs. programmed streams, saves, playlist adds, skips, follows, recency/frequency/intensity per listener
Buyer interface: Campaigns tab in Spotify for Artists (desktop, Admin/Editor roles) - campaign creation, audience-segment selection, market selection (40+ markets), scheduling, billing management
Marquee explicitly targets listeners based on their listening history rather than broad demographics or interests

Rebuildable: the segmentation logic is trivially replicable in a spreadsheet or self-hosted analytics from any first-party listener data; an indie team can manually approximate Marquee's targeting by exporting Spotify for Artists audience data and running segmented email/DM campaigns - but it will never reach 'potential listeners' Spotify has not identified to you, which is the whole point
